transcript: The other day, I saw Sally & Tom at The Public, a new play by Suzan-Lori Parks about a theater company putting on an original play about Thomas Jefferson and Sally Hemings. The play seamlessly intertwines scenes from the characters’ real lives and the scenes that those characters are putting on in their own play. I think this is a very timely piece because of the ways it questions how we're supposed to be dramatizing history, and what better place to have that conversation than in a play itself? This play does incorporate some heavy topics, I guess that's a bit of a given when looking at American history, but this is also a bit of a love letter to scrappy theater making and how art impacts our interpersonal relationships for better or for worse. It definitely has its funny moments. Do I think this holds a flame to some other pieces by Suzan-Lori Parks, such as her brilliant Pulitzer winner Topdog /Underdog? Not really —I think this is an interesting and ambitious piece but the dialogue wasn't quite as distinctive as I thought it would be and I also wish the pacing was a little tighter. I think it would have packed more of a punch if it moved maybe 15 to 20% faster but still I was otherwise mostly into this, as someone who really does not like history in general. With that, another playbill for my collection.
